Chlor. * Full text (45 Ko) * Red and blue only * Red only

   

MIND. [1] [Chlor.]
Mind tranquil and active.
Apprehension.
A horrible state of mind, fears he will go crazy, fears he cannot make a living.
Everything seems in confusion.
Cannot remember names if he sees people, and when seeing the names does not remember the person.
Quiet delirium in alternation with the greatest restlessness and desire to run away. θ Typhus.
Restless desire to walk about, as if whole attention must be centered on act of respiration.
Intoxicated feeling with sopor and great nervous irritation ; dry mouth and diarrhœa. θ Typhus.
Inclined to anger.
After excitement. θ Spasmus glottidis.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Chlor.]
Disposition to faint. θ Typhus.
Vertigo and stupor.
Coma, fainting and cold, viscous sweats. θ Typhus. θ Scarlatina. θ Measles. θ Variola.
Partially comatose during suffocative attack.
Partial unconsciousness, followed by free respiration and deep sleep.
   

INNER HEAD. [3] [Chlor.]
Rush of blood to head.
Painful aching in vertex and down left side, with inclination to lie down.
   

OUTER HEAD. [4] [Chlor.]
Warm sweat breaks out on forehead while coughing.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Chlor.]
Dull and glassy expression of eyes. θ Spasmus glottidis.
Staring eyes.
Dimness before eyes.
Running of tears < in open air.
Eyes protrude with coryza, sunken face and spasmodic cough.
Purulent ophthalmia.
   

HEARING AND EARS. [6] [Chlor.]
Singing in ears.
Deafness. θ Typhus.
   

SMELL AND NOSE. [7] [Chlor.]
Dryness in nose before coryza.
Nose smoky or sooty. θ Typhus.
Corrosive feeling in corners of nose.
Nose completely stopped.
Sudden running in drops, of a sharp, corroding fluid, with tears in eyes, dry tongue, palate and fauces.
Nose discharged mucus freely.
Water dropped from left nostril, did not burn or excoriate skin.
Coryza with headache.
Fluid coryza very soon changes to yellow, copious phlegm.
Evening coryza, morning sneezing.
Severe sneezing.
Nasal complaints < lying down.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Chlor.]
Face pale and bloated. θ Spasmus glottidis.
Pale, dirty yellow, cadaverous color ; face puffed up.
Face high colored.
Child became livid. θ Spasm of glottis.
Face extremely livid, blue.
Ash-colored face. θ Typhus.
Swollen face, with protrusion of eyes, abundant discharge of mucus from nostrils.
Warm sweat broke out on forehead while coughing.
   

LOWER FACE. [9] [Chlor.]
Lips, tongue and teeth brown, black and sooty. θ Typhus.
   

TEETH AND GUMS. [10] [Chlor.]
Sensation as if teeth were too full, or had been injured by acids.
Teeth black.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Chlor.]
Tongue dry. θ Typhus.
Sensation as if tongue had been burnt.
Tongue black.
   

INNER MOUTH. [12] [Chlor.]
Dryness of whole buccal cavity. θ Typhus.
Abundant discharge of mucus from mouth and nose.
Salivation.
Soreness of mouth, fauces and œsophagus, as if tongue had been burnt ; as if he had been eating vegetable acids, or as if his teeth had been injured by acids.
Sore mouth.
Increased vascularity and minute ulcerations in mouth and throat.
Opening mouth to take food or drink produced spasm of glottis.
Putrid odor from mouth. θ Stomacace.
   

PALATE AND THROAT. [13] [Chlor.]
Dryness of throat.
Inability to swallow.
Throat sore from uvula to bronchi, including fauces and œsophagus.
Throat and chest sore, voice hoarse.
Any attempt to examine the throat produced spasm of glottis.
Reported to have had a favorable effect upon the diphtheritic process.
   

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Chlor.]
Loss of appetite. θ Spasmus glottidis.
No thirst with coryza, but cold water is very serviceable.
   

EATING AND DRINKING. [15] [Chlor.]
Even tasting food was prevented by spasm of glottis ; while eating, and after it, hot feelings ; irritable, and disposed to get into a rage.
After eating, increase of headache with fever.
Smoking causes a dryness in mouth.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Chlor.]
Disposition to vomit.
Desire to vomit when coughing, without nausea.
Violent vomiting of dark liver-colored masses of blood, without any pain, lessening pain in precordia and sensation of suffocation.
